<description>
`unsigned` is a 32-bit integer (even on 64-bit platforms). File sizes are generally measured in 64-bit integers and using 32-bit integers or architecture-dependent integers is brittle and confusing.

So use u64 consistently for flatfile sizes in this refactor.

Also, use `LARGE_INTEGER`'s `QuadPart` on Windows, which is recommended since C++11.

Also, unit test VarInt overflow errors.
</description>

File sizes are generally measured in 64-bit integers and using 32-bit
integers or architecture-dependent integers is brittle and confusing.

faed02f6d0 refactor: Use LARGE_INTEGER QuadPart on Windows

Now that C++11 added 64-bit integers, follow
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-nz/windows/win32/api/winnt/ns-winnt-large_integer-r1#remarks

[quoted text omitted]

fa2c8df181 Add test coverage for varint overflow

Stuff like CBlockIndex::nUndoPos or CBlockFileInfo::nUndoSize is
serialized as VARINT. However, there is no test coverage at all for
VarInt overflow behavior, so add test coverage for both overflow cases
(and distinguish their error msg).
</commits>
